sources.title: Go byte-valued strings and hexadecimal byte escapes
sources.sections_read: Date; What is a string?; Printing strings; UTF-8 and string literals; Code points, characters, and runes; Range loops
sources.confirmed: Go strings can contain arbitrary bytes, support hexadecimal byte escapes, and yield individual bytes through indexing. Its quoted source literals normally use UTF-8, while explicit byte escapes can construct invalid UTF-8; range iteration instead decodes runes.
sources.limits: Ordinary source characters are UTF-8 encoded; high raw bytes need byte escapes, rune literals denote Unicode code points, and range iteration decodes runes rather than providing byte-wise traversal. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C18.json.

sources.title: Python bytes literals and integer-valued binary sequences
sources.sections_read: String and Bytes literals; prefixes; formal grammar; escape-sequence table; Bytes literals; hexadecimal and octal escapes; raw bytes literals
sources.confirmed: Python b/B-prefixed literals construct bytes instead of str, permit readable ASCII, and use explicit numeric escapes for high bytes and NUL; raw bytes literals preserve backslashes. No whole-value Unicode validity is required.
sources.limits: A one-character bytes literal is still a sequence, and indexing yields an integer rather than a dedicated byte-character literal; the successfully opened reference is later evidence because older documentation fetches failed. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C18.json.

sources.title: OCaml 4.01 eight-bit characters and shared character/string escape syntax
sources.version_or_date: OCaml 4.01 manual, dated 2013-09-12 by opened manual index
sources.sections_read: Character literals; String literals; shared escape grammar/table
sources.confirmed: Single-quoted character literals and double-quoted string literals share readable characters and explicit decimal/hexadecimal escapes.
sources.limits: The archived manual assigns ISO-8859-1 interpretation to values 128..255, so transferring this design to encoding-neutral bytes should retain the numeric representation while avoiding that text interpretation. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C18.json.

sources.title: values.html
sources.version_or_date: OCaml 4.01 manual, dated 2013-09-12 by opened manual index
sources.sections_read: Base values: Characters and Character strings
sources.confirmed: Characters are 8-bit values in 0..255 and strings are sequences of these values. The implementation interprets high character codes as ISO-8859-1, which is a transfer caveat for an encoding-neutral byte design.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C18.json.

sources.title: Nim single-byte character literals and byte-preserving strings
sources.sections_read: Character literals and escapes; Character type; String type and indexing; cstring caveat; generation footer
sources.confirmed: Nim single-quoted character literals denote single bytes and share hexadecimal/decimal escapes with strings. Strings do not enforce their UTF-8 convention and can contain binary byte sequences; indexing returns char, while Rune is a separate Unicode representation.
sources.limits: UTF-8 remains a convention for strings, so consumers must choose byte indexing rather than Unicode iteration; this development manual is later evidence and is not proof of availability before the cutoff. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C18.json.

sources.title: stdtypes.html
sources.sections_read: Bytes indexing versus slicing; Bytearray objects
sources.confirmed: Bytes objects are sequences of integers: indexing returns an integer while slicing returns bytes. Bytearray is mutable and constructed by function call rather than dedicated literal syntax.
